// PerfP521Probe times the P-521 generator-table build in its start-up role: crypto/tls's test
// package parses a P-521 ECDSA key at start, and the first ScalarBaseMult builds the table.
package main

import (
	"crypto/x509"
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"time"
)

// The two keys of crypto/tls handshake_test.go: testECDSAPrivateKey (P-521) and testP256PrivateKey.
const p521Key = ""
const p256Key = "30770201010420012f3b52bc54c36ba3577ad45034e2e8efe1e6999851284cb848725cfe029991a00a06082a8648ce3d030107a14403420004c02c61c9b16283bbcc14956d886d79b358aa614596975f78cece787146abf74c2d5dc578c0992b4f3c631373479ebf3892efe53d21c4f4f1cc9a11c3536b7f75"

func parse(der []byte) int64 {
	t := time.Now()
	if _, err := x509.ParseECPrivateKey(der); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	return time.Since(t).Nanoseconds()
}

func main() {
	n := 50
	if len(os.Args) > 1 {
		n, _ = strconv.Atoi(os.Args[1])
	}
	p521, _ := hex.DecodeString(p521Key)
	p256, _ := hex.DecodeString(p256Key)

	// P-256 first, so one-time ECDSA set-up is outside the P-521 numbers.
	p256First := parse(p256)
	first := parse(p521)
	second := parse(p521)
	steady := make([]int64, n)
	for i := range steady {
		steady[i] = parse(p521)
	}
	sort.Slice(steady, func(i, j int) bool { return steady[i] < steady[j] })
	fmt.Printf("p256_first_us %d p521_first_us %d p521_second_us %d p521_steady_median_us %d n %d\n",
		p256First/1000, first/1000, second/1000, steady[n/2]/1000, n)
}
